chunks: ʿAlī ibn al-Nuʿmān and Ṣafwān narrated from Yaḥyā al-Azraq, who said:

I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man performing saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, who completes three circuits or four, then a friend meets him and invites him to attend to a need or to food.

He عليه السلام said: “If he responds to him, there is no harm in that, but that he fulfill the right of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is more beloved to me than that he fulfill the right of his companion.”

key_terms.أَشْوَاطٍ: circuits or laps of the saʿy
key_terms.الصَّفَا: al-Ṣafā, one of the two points of saʿy in hajj and ʿumrah rites
key_terms.الْحَاجَةِ: a need or errand requiring attention
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: al-Marwah, the other endpoint of the saʿy rite
key_terms.حَقَّ اللَّهِ: the right due to Allah, referring here to the act of worship being completed
key_terms.حَقَّ صَاحِبِهِ: the right of his companion or friend
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permitted
key_terms.يَسْعَى: performs saʿy, the ritual walking between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah

ai.seo_question: Can a person interrupt saʿy between Ṣafā and Marwah to respond to a friend or go for food?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on interrupting saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah for a worldly need or social invitation. The Imam عليه السلام permits it without declaring it blameworthy, while making clear that completing the duty owed to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is preferable. It thus combines a legal allowance with an ethical preference for prioritizing acts of worship.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2856 - Ali ibn al-Nu'man and Safwan narrated from Yahya al-Azraq, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (as) about a man performing Sa'i (ritual walking) between Safa and Marwah. If he completes three or four circuits and then meets a friend who invites him to fulfill a need or to have food, what should he do?
Imam (as) replied: "If he responds to him, there is no harm in it, but fulfilling the right of Allah (swt), the Almighty, is more beloved to me than fulfilling the right of his companion."
